title: Escharotomy
stem: Resus 3. A 40-year-old man with 45% burns from a factory fire was intubated two hours ago and is waiting for transfer to the burns centre. The nurse calls you: the ventilator is alarming and his saturation is falling. He has full-thickness burns around his whole chest and his right arm.

phases.title: DOPES
phases.goal: The ventilator is alarming: work through the causes yourself before blaming the eschar.

phases.title: Chest escharotomy
phases.goal: By hand: both sides and the costal margin, into fat; then the arm.

phases.title: The call
phases.goal: The ischaemic arm, then tell the burns centre.

review.text: Chest incisions. Your notes join them 'at the sternum and pubis'. The standard chest escharotomy joins the two anterior axillary incisions along the costal margin (a 'shield'). An abdominal extension is added only if the abdomen is burned and tight too.

notes:
Checked against ATLS 11th edition, British Burn Association guidance on escharotomy, and ANZBA EMSB principles.

Full-thickness eschar is inelastic. As tissue swells under a circumferential eschar, the chest cannot expand (high airway pressures, hypercapnia, falling saturation) and limbs become ischaemic (loss of Doppler signal, cool, delayed capillary refill; pain and paraesthesia in an awake patient).

Before blaming the eschar in a ventilated patient, run DOPES: Displacement of the tube, Obstruction (secretions, soot), Pneumothorax, Equipment, Stacking of breaths.

Chest: bilateral incisions in the anterior axillary lines from the clavicle to the costal margin, joined by a transverse incision along the costal margin to make a 'shield' that moves with breathing. Your notes say to join them 'at the sternum and pubis'; the standard join for the chest is subcostal (an abdominal extension is added only when the abdomen is also burned and tight).

Limbs: mid-medial and mid-lateral lines along the whole length of the eschar, avoiding the ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle and the common peroneal nerve at the fibular head. Hands: dorsal incisions between the metacarpals; fingers: mid-lateral, away from the pinch surfaces.

Depth: through the eschar into subcutaneous fat until the edges gape, not through fascia. Electrical injury damages muscle under the skin and may need a fasciotomy; that is a surgical procedure. Your notes' indications, timing (usually within 6 hours) and contraindications match this.

Perfect script checked against an ATLS/EMSB checklist, BBA escharotomy guidance, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the wrong options (raising the pressure limit, paralysing, a tenfold dose, not telling the burns centre) and the bench's 'through fascia into muscle' button. Added: DOPES summarised aloud, the ventilator reading scored.

steps.label: Assess
steps.hint: Rule out tube and ventilator causes (DOPES) before the eschar.

Tube.t: Tube position at the teeth; capnography trace
Tube.r: Tube at 23 cm as documented. Square ETCO2 trace, 7.2 kPa.

Tube.t: Pass a suction catheter down the tube
Tube.r: Passes easily. A little sooty sputum.

Chest.r: Barely moves. Full-thickness, leathery eschar all the way round. "A circumferential chest eschar."
Chest.mark: Finds a circumferential full-thickness chest eschar

Chest.r: Quiet but equal air entry. Lung sliding on both sides.

Ventilator.r: Very stiff to bag. The problem stays off the ventilator.
Peak pressure 44 cmH2O (was 24). Tidal volume falling. No breath stacking.
Ventilator.mark: Reads the ventilator: high peak pressure, no breath stacking

Right arm.t: Pulses and capillary refill, right hand
Right arm.r: No radial or ulnar Doppler signal. Hand cool, capillary refill 5 s. Full-thickness burn all round the arm.
Right arm.mark: Finds an ischaemic limb under circumferential eschar

steps.label: Talk to the nurse
steps.hint: Say the indication and do it now; tell the burns centre.

opts.t: DOPES is clear: the tube is in and patent, no pneumothorax, the problem stays off the ventilator, no stacking. It's the circumferential chest eschar restricting ventilation.
opts.mark: Summarises DOPES and names the cause

opts.t: Chest escharotomy now, at the bedside, then the right arm for the ischaemic hand.
opts.mark: States the indication and prioritises the chest

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Top up analgesia and sedation before you cut.

opts.mark: Analgesia and sedation (the edges are sensate)

steps.label: Escharotomy
steps.hint: Prepare; mark both anterior axillary lines and the costal margin; cut into fat; diathermy; recheck; then the arm.

opts.performHint: Do it with your hands. Watch the airway pressure as you cut.
mark: Joins them along the costal margin (chest shield)
Incises through eschar only, to subcutaneous fat
Limb escharotomy on the mid-axial lines, avoiding the ulnar nerve

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: Tell the burns centre what you did and why.

opts.t: Burns centre: Mr Siu's chest and right arm escharotomies are done, for ventilation and an ischaemic hand. Airway pressure is down and the Doppler signals are back.
opts.r: Burns registrar: Thank you. Keep elevating the arm; transfer as planned.

wrong: Drugs, Oxygen supply, Pressure alarm, Eschar, Sedation

qs.a: Through the eschar to subcutaneous fat
wrong: Down to bone, through the periosteum
Through the deep fascia into the muscle compartments

qs.q: Which burn more often needs a fasciotomy rather than an escharotomy?
qs.why: Current travels through muscle, which swells beneath intact-looking skin.
wrong: Scald to both hands of a toddler
Flash burn to the face and neck

qs.q: Which nerve is at risk on the medial side of the elbow?

wrong: Down the middle of the palm
Over the dorsum of each knuckle

badge.name: Shield Maker
badge.flavor: DOPES first. Then free the chest along the axillary lines.

options: Anterior axillary lines, joined at the costal margin
Down the midline sternum from notch to xiphoid
Both mid-clavicular lines, joined across the clavicles
Transversely below the nipples, from axilla to axilla
cards.why: The 'shield' releases the chest wall to move with breathing.

cards.q: Sign of a tight chest eschar in a ventilated patient?
options: Rising peak airway pressures and hypercapnia
Falling peak airway pressures
Bradycardia with a narrow pulse pressure
Polyuria and a rising serum sodium
cards.why: The rigid shell restricts chest expansion.

options: Mid-medial and mid-lateral
Along the anterior midline
Along the posterior midline
A spiral around the limb
cards.why: They release the circumference while sparing tendons and nerves.

cards.q: Why is an escharotomy often painless in the middle but painful at the edges?
options: Full thickness is insensate; edges are partial thickness
The patient is always paralysed and deeply sedated for it
Burnt skin releases endorphins that block local pain
Subcutaneous fat has no sensory nerve supply at all
cards.why: Give analgesia: the unburnt and partial-thickness margins hurt.

cards.q: An intubated burns patient desaturates. First step?
options: DOPES check
Chest escharotomy at once
Increase PEEP to 20
Give furosemide
cards.why: Rule out tube displacement, obstruction, pneumothorax, equipment and stacking.

cards.q: Circumferential full-thickness burn of the arm with no Doppler signal. Action?
options: Escharotomy of the arm
Elevate and review in 24 hours
Apply a tourniquet
Wrap it tightly with cling film
cards.why: Ischaemia under a constricting eschar needs release.

script.say: DOPES. Displacement: the tube is at 23 cm with a square capnography trace. Obstruction: a suction catheter passes easily. Pneumothorax: equal air entry and lung sliding on both sides. Equipment: off the ventilator he's still very stiff to bag. Stacking: none; peak pressure 44, up from 24.
The chest barely moves: a circumferential, full-thickness eschar. The right hand: no Doppler signal, cool, refill 5 seconds: an ischaemic limb under a circumferential eschar.

DOPES is clear: the tube is in and patent, no pneumothorax, the problem stays off the ventilator, no stacking. It's the circumferential chest eschar restricting ventilation. Chest escharotomy now, at the bedside, then the right arm for the ischaemic hand.
Fentanyl 1 microgram per kg, 70 micrograms, before I cut: the edges are sensate.
Sterile prep and diathermy. Mark both anterior axillary lines, clavicle to costal margin, joined along the costal margin: a shield. Cut through the eschar into fat until the edges gape.

Haemostasis with diathermy, dressing. Reassess ventilation. Then the right arm: mid-medial and mid-lateral lines along the whole eschar, avoiding the ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle. Doppler signals back.
Burns centre: Mr Siu's chest and right arm escharotomies are done, for ventilation and an ischaemic hand. Airway pressure is down and the Doppler signals are back.
